nodes.text: The guards let you through, which means you climbed the High Road on your own feet. Come in, then. The Line has always had time for people who arrive the hard way.
Ask. I'm told kings are supposed to make people wait. My grandfather was a quarry foreman — waiting wastes daylight.

choices.text: Why open the Undercroft after twenty years?

nodes.text: Five kings, one name. The first Aeriex was a quarry foreman who paid the shepherds' debts in silver, and got called *king* for it — half as a joke. He kept the half that wasn't. The bargain hasn't changed since: the Crown pays first, pays fairest, and keeps the roads lit. The day an Aeriex breaks it, the mountain will find another foreman. It found the first one.

I outrank everything on this mountain except the mountain. Maren speaks for the mountain. She was Castellan under my father; she'll be Castellan under my heir, if she consents to it. When she says a gallery is unsafe, it closes before I've finished nodding. That's not weakness. That's knowing what my throne is bolted to.

choices.text: You know about the Rookery, don't you.

nodes.text: _A king who claims his city has no shadows is announcing he's stopped looking at it._ Yes. Behind the bank, past the scree. The Magpie's people were quarrymen before my family were kings — they have the older claim, if we're honest about it, and a king should occasionally be. They watch what my watch can't. I leave them their dark, and the dark stays civil.

Twenty years my father kept his grief sealed behind good stonework, and the kobolds dug on regardless. Maren came to me with the surveys and said: *the seal keeps out miners, not monsters.* I gave the order the same hour. If the deep is going to be contested, I'd rather contest it with the lamps lit.
And a good road to you. Mind the edge — royal decree.
